intro_script: Welcome to your daily Robotics digest from November 23, 2026. Today we cover big news, including Genesis AI's funding, a laundry robot success, and advances in autonomous driving.
outro_script: And that's all the circuits for today! Genesis AI just powered up a massive funding round. Thanks for plugging into the future with me. Until tomorrow, keep building brilliantly!

items.title: Genesis AI raises $500 million to scale general-purpose robotics
items.summary: Genesis AI raised $500 million in Series A funding at a $3.5 billion valuation to advance general-purpose robotics. The company plans to use the funds to expand robot production, enhance data collection, and recruit personnel. Genesis is increasing production of its general-purpose robot, Eno, targeting expansion into new sectors like hospitality and healthcare. The company develops an integrated platform, including the GENE AI foundation model and the Genesis World simulation platform. Long-term, Genesis aims to create robots capable of autonomous, multi-step tasks across various environments.

This investment signals a significant push toward tangible, general-purpose physical automation.

items.title: Gobano Robotics reports 99.5 percent success rate for autonomous laundry robot
items.summary: Gobano Robotics reports a 99.5 percent success rate for its autonomous laundry robot at Henri Wartner Group. The system handles repetitive towel folding and inspection tasks autonomously for several hours. It achieves 68 percent of a human worker's throughput over an 18-hour shift through reinforcement learning. The robot can automatically recover from grasp failures to maintain production flow without constant human supervision. Gobano uses production data to continuously improve the robot's performance and plans further expansion of its capabilities.

items.title: Kakao Mobility partners with Nvidia to develop Level 4 autonomous driving technology
items.summary: Kakao Mobility and Nvidia signed an agreement to develop Level 4 autonomous driving technology, initially targeting Kia's purpose-built vehicles. The partnership will merge Kakao Mobility's autonomous driving software with Nvidia's computing, sensor, and safety technologies. Kakao Mobility plans to develop a high-performance computing unit using Nvidia Drive AGX Thor processors and Hyperion architecture. This collaboration aims to establish the technical foundation for driverless mobility services in South Korea. The partnership seeks to advance end-to-end AI technology and prepare for Level 4 commercialization.

items.title: Remedy Robotics raises $62 million to advance AI-powered cardiovascular surgery robot
items.summary: Remedy Robotics raised $62 million in Series B funding to advance its AI-enabled N1 System for cardiovascular and neurovascular procedures. This funding will support clinical trials, regulatory approval, and further development of the robotic platform for remote and potentially autonomous endovascular operations. The N1 System uses robotics, machine learning, and computer vision to analyze imaging and simulate procedures. Remedy plans pivotal clinical trials with the University of California as it pursues FDA approval for neurovascular intervention. The company aims to expand access to specialist treatment globally through its robotic system.

items.title: Nvidia expands Isaac robotics platform with new humanoid and AI development tools
items.summary: Nvidia expanded its Isaac robotics platform by introducing new simulation frameworks, AI training tools, datasets, and a reference humanoid robot. This expansion includes the Agile ONE SN platform from Agile Robots, which integrates Nvidia's Isaac GR00T foundation model and Jetson Thor. Nvidia also released Isaac OS and Isaac Lab 3.0, along with resources like the Human 1M Dataset for robot learning. European robotics companies are actively integrating these Nvidia technologies into their development platforms. These developments underscore the industry trend of combining foundation models, simulation, and hardware for more adaptable autonomous systems.

items.title: Mitsubishi Electric expands US manufacturing and technology investments to $2.9 billion
items.summary: Mitsubishi Electric has committed over $2.9 billion in US investments, acquisitions, and commitments over the last two years. These investments include $259.5 million in manufacturing facilities across Kentucky, Pennsylvania, and Ohio, creating over 400 jobs. The company is also expanding into software and cybersecurity through planned acquisitions and a new digital transformation hub. Specific projects include expanding switchgear manufacturing and data-center cooling operations. Overall, the strategy aims to strengthen US manufacturing while expanding capabilities in energy, cybersecurity, and artificial intelligence.

items.title: Schunk spin-off Tactilia Robotics launches to develop dexterous robot hands
items.summary: Schunk has launched Tactilia Robotics, a Munich-based company developing modular robotic hands for industrial automation. The goal is to create hands capable of reliably gripping and manipulating objects across various robot platforms. The development integrates mechanical engineering, sensors, actuators, software, and physical AI to achieve human-like dexterity. Tactilia's modular approach allows adaptation to different industrial applications without manufacturer restrictions. The company prioritizes developing reliable robotic hands for practical integration in industrial settings.

items.title: Multiway Robotics showcases wheeled humanoid and autonomous forklifts at CeMAT Asia 2026
items.summary: Multiway Robotics displayed five autonomous material handling solutions at CeMAT Asia 2026, including a wheeled humanoid robot. Their lineup featured specialized vehicles like an omnidirectional sideloader, a narrow-aisle forklift, an autonomous pallet truck, and a counterbalanced forklift. The wheeled humanoid robot demonstrated mobile manipulation capabilities for flexible handling in manufacturing and warehousing. Autonomous forklifts were showcased for specific tasks such as heavy transport, high-density warehousing access, and precision stacking. Multiway also presented integrated software platforms to coordinate these autonomous vehicles with warehouse operations.

items.title: Boston Dynamics gives Atlas wheels to test new reinforcement learning capabilities
items.summary: Boston Dynamics tested reinforcement learning by temporarily equipping its Atlas humanoid robot with wheels to explore new movement capabilities. Engineers attached scooter rims to the robot's ankle actuators to evaluate motor performance under varied speed and torque demands. This experiment aimed to bridge the gap between simulated behaviors and real-world physical hardware. The research involved combining motor control with reinforcement learning to develop more robust control systems. The ultimate goal is to enhance Atlas's reliability in real-world environments rather than creating a wheeled robot.

The research involved combining motor control with reinforcement learning to develop more robust control systems, aiming to enhance Atlas's reliability in real-world environments rather than creating a fully wheeled robot. This methodology focused on assessing the interaction between motor control and learned behaviors in physical motion. The findings suggest a pathway for improving the adaptability and reliability of advanced robotic systems in physical settings.

items.title: Topstar unveils Star humanoid for factory handling tasks
items.summary: Topstar introduced Star, a 172 cm tall, 72 kg bipedal humanoid for factory material handling and sorting at TOPS DAY 2026. The company also features Xiaotuo, a wheeled humanoid, which is being tested for similar manufacturing applications. Development priorities for Star include sorting varied products, multi-tasking at workstations, and intelligent material handling.

items.title: BlueBotics unifies fleet management for manual forklifts and mobile robots
items.summary: BlueBotics updated its ANT locator system to unify fleet management for manual forklifts and mobile robots. This update introduces unified mission dispatch, allowing the ANT server software to assign tasks to AGVs, AMRs, and forklifts based on real-time location and availability. The system features an in-cab interface for forklift operators to manage assignments and coordinates movement between manual and automated vehicles. This coordination helps prevent traffic congestion and improve the use of warehouse space through shared space awareness. Furthermore, the system supports pallet tracking and provides analytics like heatmaps to identify operational inefficiencies.

items.title: Soft Robot Made for the Races
items.summary: A recent UC San Diego study showed a slight increase in land speed records for soft robotics. This achievement utilized pneumatic logic gates for actuation, enabling quick cycling between abduction and adduction rather than direct microcontroller control. The compliant oscillations in the robots also allow for the use of other fluids like water. Although the robot was 3D printed using TPE, further development is suggested using silicone. This research highlights the evolving capabilities within the field of soft robotics.
items.audio_script: From Hackaday - Robots, "Soft Robot Made for the Races". This story details a recent study indicating a slight increase in land speed records achieved by soft robotics. The research employed pneumatic logic gates for actuation, which facilitated rapid cycling between abduction and adduction instead of relying on direct microcontroller control. The robots demonstrated compliant oscillations that permit the use of alternative fluids such as water in their operation. The physical construction of the robot utilized three-dimensional printing with thermoplastic elastomer, although further development is suggested focusing on silicone materials for future iterations. This research demonstrates the evolving capabilities within the field of soft robotics. This work points toward continued advancements in adaptable and fluid-driven robotic systems.

items.title: One Behavior, Out of Order: Deterministic Execution and Parallel Simulation of ROS 2 Applications
items.summary: ROS 2 applications suffer from nondeterminism due to asynchronous communication, making tests unreliable. A coordination scheme is introduced to make ROS 2 applications deterministic by enforcing predefined read and write time instants for all components. An out-of-order parallel simulation algorithm is then developed to speed up testing based on these time instants. This method is implemented in a simulator that runs existing ROS 2 applications without modification. The simulation proves to be significantly faster and more memory-efficient than other parallel simulation methods.

items.title: Latent Space Planning with Sequential Monte Carlo
items.summary: Planning with learned world models involves finding action sequences that achieve a goal, where sampling-based methods and gradient-based methods face limitations. Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) is utilized to naturally evolve a sequence of intermediate distributions in this context through importance weighting and resampling. The method formulates latent-space planning as optimization guided by SMC, where a gradient-based optimizer refines the plan. This approach outperforms other methods on navigation and manipulation tasks by significantly improving the success rate.

items.title: FORTH: Grounding Tactile VLA Execution via Forward-Only Proxy-Control Pairing
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies assume proxy loss minimization grounds tactile execution, but this assumption fails due to mismatches at different deployment levels. FORTH introduces a forward-only measurement harness to explicitly pair optimization objectives with physical control observables. It incorporates a tactile encoder, a zeroth-order adapter, and a SlipGuard gate to achieve grounded execution. This method results in superior performance, achieving a 97.6% success rate and reducing activation memory significantly compared to backpropagated methods. Ultimately, FORTH enhances physical intelligence by enabling deeper perception.

items.title: MomentMem: Memorizing Key Moments for Robot Manipulation
items.summary: Visual moment memory focuses on retaining key visual details from specific moments to aid robot manipulation. MomentMem proposes a hierarchical architecture where a Vision-Language Model selects keyframes and an executor predicts actions based on these memories. This separation allows for evaluating memory selection independently of action execution. MomentMem achieved 49.9% success on the VMBench tasks, outperforming baselines by a significant margin. The method demonstrates the value of retaining sparse visual evidence for memory-dependent robotic tasks.

items.title: Search-Informed MPPI for Kinodynamic Motion Planning via Monte Carlo Tree Expansion
items.summary: Kinodynamic motion planning in cluttered environments is challenging due to the need for dynamically feasible, collision-free trajectories over long horizons. Search-Informed MPPI (SI-MPPI) is proposed as a framework to combine Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) optimization with Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) for this task. It fuses MCTS expansion and default-policy simulation into an MPPI expansion guided by "baits" for GPU-batched trajectory optimization. Feasibility gating and cost-based backpropagation are used to guide sparse tree growth in the MCTS process. Simulations show SI-MPPI produces smoother control profiles and smaller search trees than baselines while maintaining competitive planning performance.

items.title: TacHOI: Contact-Aware Object Reconstruction and Tracking for Egocentric Videos
items.summary: TacHOI is a training-free framework that reconstructs and tracks objects in egocentric videos by integrating tactile contact with monocular vision. It uses tactile contact to constrain object depth relative to the hand, leveraging spatially separated contacts on the hand as a physical ruler for object extent. The method jointly optimizes hand poses, object trajectories, and anisotropic object scale alongside visual alignment. Experiments on ARCTIC and HO3D sequences showed significant error reduction, achieving 3.6 cm and 2.8 cm errors respectively. This approach demonstrates applicability when measured tactile observations are available.

items.title: LoCo-WAM: Test-Time Training as Long Context for World-Action Models
items.summary: LoCo-WAM introduces test-time training to use longer context for world-action models by learning from action outcomes without expert labels. It updates a low-rank adapter in the video expert using newly observed frames while maintaining the original short history length. These updates accumulate within episodes and reset between them, allowing past observations to influence decisions outside the input window. Experiments demonstrate that this method improves task success across simulation benchmarks. The learned updates enhance prediction of future frames and actions, with their effect on actions increasing as the episode progresses.
